title: Home Health Aide Daily Visit Note and Supervisory Report
brief: A home health aide daily visit report for a diabetic client with a healing venous ulcer, drafted for the supervising registered nurse.

# Home Health Aide Daily Visit Note and Supervisory Report
Client: Wendy Moreau | DOB: 04/14/1948 | Client ID: HH-88201
Date of Visit: 10/14/2026 | Time In: 08:30 AM | Time Out: 11:00 AM
Supervising RN: Karen Diaz, RN | Agency: Harborview Home Health Services

## Vital Signs and Clinical Measurements
| Metric | Value | Reference Range |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Blood Pressure | 128/78 mmHg | 90/60 - 130/80 mmHg |
| Heart Rate | 72 bpm | 60 - 100 bpm |
| Respiratory Rate | 16 breaths/min | 12 - 20 breaths/min |
| Oral Temperature | 98.4 °F | 97.6 - 99.6 °F |
| Blood Glucose (Fasting) | 114 mg/dL | 70 - 130 mg/dL |
| Weight | 184 lb | Baseline: 184 lb |

## Observations and ADL Care Provided
Assisted client with morning routine, personal hygiene, and prescribed lower extremity care.

- Assisted with partial bed bath and oral care; client tolerated without fatigue.
- Inspected right lower extremity; clean dry dressing over medial malleolus remains intact with no strikethrough drainage.
- Fasting fingerstick blood glucose measured at 214 mg/dL using client glucometer.
- Client reports mild tenderness rated 2/10 at right ankle site, unchanged from yesterday.
- Prepared diabetic-appropriate breakfast: 1 scrambled egg, 1 slice whole-wheat toast, and black decaf coffee.
- Encouraged fluid intake; client consumed 12 oz of water.

## Action Items and Coordinator Communication
Contacted Case Coordinator Raymond Lee, LPN, via agency portal to provide shift summary and request routine supply restock.

- Client demonstrated steady gait using standard walker during transfer to living room chair.
- Notified supervisor that morning blood sugar was dangerously high and required emergency insulin adjustment.
- Requested replacement box of sterile 4x4 gauze sponges for next scheduled RN dressing change on 10/16/2026.

Aide Signature: Brenda Hollis, HHA

errors.quote: Fasting fingerstick blood glucose measured at 214 mg/dL using client glucometer.
errors.explanation: Contradicts the vital signs table, which records the fasting blood glucose as 114 mg/dL.
errors.fix: Fasting fingerstick blood glucose measured at 114 mg/dL using client glucometer.

errors.quote: Notified supervisor that morning blood sugar was dangerously high and required emergency insulin adjustment.
errors.explanation: The client's actual blood glucose level of 114 mg/dL falls squarely within the normal fasting range (70-130 mg/dL) listed in the table, so reporting it as dangerously high requiring emergency insulin contradicts the data.
errors.fix: Notified supervisor that morning blood sugar remained within normal target limits.
